defects: The 'N' in the SIGNAL wordmark looks like an 'M', so the title reads as 'SIGMAL' in every frame
From about 2.5 s to 5.0 s nothing moves except typewriter characters and a blinking cursor. That is dead air across roughly half the film.
The logo resolve (thin scanlines thickening into bars) is one linear move with no ease, overshoot or settle. It completes inside the first second and is never touched again.
Characters type at an even rate with no human or machine rhythm: no pauses, bursts or line-feed beats. The handshake progress bar appears already full instead of filling.
The glow is a uniform Gaussian bloom on flat pure-black. There is no phosphor texture, scanline field, vignette, flicker or curvature, so the 'CRT' look reads as a CSS text-shadow.
The bottom two-thirds of the frame stays mostly empty. The composition never changes after the first second.
The header 'CH.03 · LOCAL 23:59' is tiny and low contrast, close to illegible at delivery size
gaps: Choreography: there is one camera-less locked-off frame and a single move. Top work would push in on the terminal, let the signal glitch, drop out and re-acquire, and build to a peak beat (the handshake connecting) around 3–4 s before releasing.

Timing and weight: the scanline resolve and the typing are both linear. They need eased acquisition (lines jitter, overshoot in thickness, then lock), rhythmic typing with holds, and a payoff moment that lands rather than just stopping on a blinking cursor.

Material finish: no phosphor grain, scanline mask, bloom falloff variation, chromatic fringing or subtle flicker. As a result the CRT conceit has no tactility at 100%, and the wordmark glyph error undermines the hero type.
